messages:
Sahana Iyer: Heads up: deploy gate *blocked* an api-gateway deploy in staging just now. It’s supposed to be soft-block only when budget is EXHAUSTED, but the dashboards show we’re fine. Anyone around to sanity check? This is the new `deployctl preflight` step.

Devon Price: I saw that too. Build link: https://ci.redwood.dev/builds/879122 (internal). The check-run output says:

```
Error Budget Gate: BLOCKED (soft-block)
service=api-gateway tier=hosted region=us-east-1 window=28d
status=EXHAUSTED
budget_remaining=-0.7%
primary_sli=availability
burn_rate_1h=12.4x burn_rate_6h=4.1x
```

But Grafana “Hosted SLO / api-gateway / us-east-1” shows ~99.95% availability and ~68% budget remaining.

Benji Okafor: That’s not great. Can you paste the raw JSON from deployctl (`--format json`)? Want to see what scope it thinks it’s querying.

Sahana Iyer: Yep:

```
{
  "service":"api-gateway",
  "tier":"hosted",
  "region":"us-east-1",
  "window":"28d",
  "status":"EXHAUSTED",
  "budget_remaining_pct_28d":"-0.7",
  "primary_sli":"availability",
  "top_contributors":["http_499","gateway_timeout"],
  "links":[
    "https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/slo-hosted-api-gateway?var-region=us-east-1",
    "https://confluence.redwood.dev/display/SRE/Error+Budget+Policy"
  ]
}
```
The “top contributors” being `http_499` smells like the old miscounting thing.

Aisha Bello: +1, `http_499` should generally be excluded from server availability for Hosted (client abort / customer-side timeouts), unless classified as server-side disconnect. We fixed this once already in SLI land, but maybe the gate service is using the wrong query.

Ethan Park: Is this coming from the control plane budget-check endpoint or is deployctl doing math locally?

Devon Price: Control plane endpoint. deployctl is just formatting. It’s hitting `/internal/error-budgets/check`.

deploy-bot: (system) Error Budget Gate (soft-block) — api-gateway hosted/us-east-1 => EXHAUSTED. Deploy blocked. Override token: not provided.

Benji Okafor: Ok. I’m looking at the control plane implementation. We might still be pulling from the “raw availability SLI” metric that includes 499/408 as failures (from the pre-hotfix definition), instead of the canonical SLI series from slo-toolkit.

Jordan Lee: Also check if we’re accidentally querying the *Dedicated* budget but printing Hosted. Policy engine has a couple of footguns around default tier when context is missing.

Sahana Iyer: I don’t think so (it prints tier=hosted and the URL it links is Hosted). But could be returning the wrong budget_id under the hood.

Nadia Rahman: Can someone share which metric name the budget job is using for availability? If gate uses `http_requests_total` directly (status class), it’ll definitely treat 499 as server error. The dashboards moved to the derived SLI series with exclusions.

Benji Okafor: Found it. The budget-check endpoint is querying the budget store, but the store record is built by the older cron job that still uses:
- `availability_good = total - (5xx + 499 + timeouts)`
Instead of the newer classification (exclude client abort 499, include only server-side disconnect/timeouts).

Aisha Bello: That lines up with the “top contributors” being `http_499` and `gateway_timeout`. We need to ensure the budget computation job uses the same SLI spec as the dashboards.

Devon Price: Why are dashboards healthy then? Are dashboards already reading from the new computation path?

Nadia Rahman: Yes — Grafana panels were updated to use `sli_success_total/sli_total` emitted by the SLI pipeline. The budget store path is lagging (still using the old rollup job). So gate is effectively blocking on a different definition than the one we blessed.

Ethan Park: That explains the mismatch. Immediate mitigation: flip the gate back to warn-only until we patch budget store, or ship a hotfix quickly.

Sahana Iyer: +1. This is blocking staging deploys. I can toggle the soft-block feature flag for api-gateway back to warn-only for now.

Jordan Lee: Do that. Policy-wise we can’t block based on inconsistent indicators. Also please add an audit note in the gate rollout ticket.

Benji Okafor: I’ll push a hotfix PR to switch the budget store computation to use the canonical SLI series / exclusions. This is basically the same fix as the earlier 499 miscount issue, but in the budget pipeline.

Aisha Bello: Link it here when up. Also we should reference the earlier hotfix so reviewers understand the context.

Benji Okafor: PR is up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/18544 — “Hotfix: correct miscounting of 499/timeout errors in Hosted availability SLI (budget store + gate)”.

Notes:
- exclude `http_499` where `disconnect_class=client_abort`
- only count `timeout_class=server` as failure
- add a unit test that the budget remaining matches dashboard computation on a known sample

Devon Price: Thank you. Once that merges, we should backfill the last 28d in the budget store or the gate will still think we’re exhausted until window rolls.

Nadia Rahman: Agree. At minimum recompute for last 7d so we can unblock quickly. Ideally full 28d recompute, but we can do it off-peak.

Benji Okafor: I’ll add a one-off recompute for Hosted/api-gateway/us-east-1 after merge. Also updating the endpoint to return `sli_definition_version` so if we ever drift again, it’s obvious.

Sahana Iyer: Soft-block flag toggled back to warn-only for api-gateway for now. Once PR is merged + recompute runs, we can re-enable soft-block.

Ethan Park: Perfect. After fix, let’s do a quick post in #eng-sre so they know why the gate was noisy and that we aligned definitions.

Aisha Bello: +1. Also please add a short note in the Confluence “release gates using error budgets” page: “Gate relies on budget store; budget store must be sourced from canonical SLI metrics; do not use raw HTTP status rollups.”
